position: CDC (Division of Reproductive Health and communications)
proposal: The Mandate recommends that CDC eliminate programs and projects that do not respect human life and conscience rights, avoid promoting abortion as health care, fund studies of the risks and complications of abortion, correct messaging on the comparative health effects of childbirth and abortion, update its public messaging on fertility awareness-based methods (and stop conflating them with older calendar methods), and fund studies of modern fertility awareness methods (pp. 454-455).
remaining: Elimination of CDC programs the Mandate characterizes as not respecting life and conscience (p. 454)
CDC-funded studies on abortion risks and complications (p. 455)
Corrected CDC messaging on childbirth versus abortion (p. 455)
Updated CDC messaging on fertility awareness-based methods and funded studies of them (p. 455)

Confidence kept at 35 because no CDC site search was made by either researcher or reviewer.
review.mandate_note: Pages 454 and 455 ask CDC to end programs that do not respect life and conscience, stop promoting abortion as health care, fund abortion-risk studies, correct childbirth versus abortion messaging, and update and fund research on fertility awareness-based methods.

After CDC cuts, doctors fear women will lose access to contraception research (team cut in April 2025 RIF)

status_summary: No CDC action matching these items was found since 2025-01-20: no announced funding for abortion-risk studies, no revised fertility awareness messaging and no program closure tied to this recommendation. A Federal Register search for fertility awareness returned only a 2026-05-13 interagency proposed rule on excepted fertility benefits, which does not concern CDC messaging. A 2025 news report described the cut of a CDC contraception guidance team in an April 2025 reduction in force, but the report does not tie it to this recommendation, so it is not counted as a qualifying action.
title: CDC: end programs conflicting with life and conscience; fund abortion-risk, FABM studies
uncertainties: Searches run: Federal Register API queries for fertility awareness and for abortion in CDC documents (the latter returned only two routine information collection notices), and one web search on CDC reproductive health cuts. The CDC website and grant listings were not searched for messaging changes or study funding, so a non-Federal Register action could have been missed. The April 2025 contraception team cut was reported by OPB and a local station without any link to this recommendation, so it is mentioned here only as context. Related records: c14-14 (abortion data reporting) and c14-07.
